name: Icinga2 Docker
what_it_is: Official Docker image for Icinga 2, the open-source monitoring framework, configurable as a master or agent node via environment variables. Bundles Icinga 2 daemon, monitoring-plugins, and several check plugins inside a Debian bookworm-slim image.
measurement: Host/service check results with performance data
configuration: ICINGA_MASTER=1 — run node as master (runs icinga2 node setup --master)
ICINGA_ZONE=<name> — zone name for agent nodes
ICINGA_ENDPOINT=<cn>,<host>,<port> — parent endpoint for agent registration
ICINGA_CACERT=<pem> — CA certificate content injected at runtime
ICINGA_TICKET=<hex> — PKI ticket for automated agent enrollment
ICINGA_PARENT_HOST / ICINGA_PARENT_ZONE — parent node connection details
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism; checks return CRITICAL/WARNING states on failure
Passive check results can be submitted via REST API to simulate any state
Node connectivity failures can be simulated by stopping the master container
modes: master — standalone or top-level monitoring node (ICINGA_MASTER=1)
agent — satellite node connecting to a parent master via PKI ticket enrollment
manual — provide pre-built config/certs in /data without running node setup
constraints: Container requires a persistent volume on /data and a stable hostname (-h flag); without these, node identity and certificates are lost on restart
Do NOT mount sub-paths under /data/etc/icinga2 or /data/var/*/icinga2 unless /data already contains all sibling directories — partial mounts break the symlink structure and corrupt the installation
icinga2 node setup runs only once per container lifetime; re-enrollment requires clearing /data or providing a fresh volume
Port 5665 must be reachable between master and agent containers; TLS certificates must be issued by the same CA
docker_services: icinga/icinga2 (single image used for both master and agent roles, distinguished by environment variables)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository — multi-container setup must be assembled manually
No Icinga Web 2 or IDO database in this image — UI and database backend require separate containers
No built-in SNMP trap receiver daemon (snmptrapd) — SNMP trap handling requires additional setup
No Grafana or metrics storage — performance data export needs external configuration
